description: Held-out challenge set, written after the detector was built and never used to tune it. For each corpus fact: one faithful PARAPHRASE (true, different wording) and one ENTITY SWAP (false: a name/object/unit is replaced, numbers unchanged). These are the two cases a lexical detector is weakest at.

items.paraphrase: Light travels through empty space at nearly 300,000 km each second, and since 1983 that figure has defined the length of a metre.
items.entity_swap: The speed of sound in a vacuum is 299,792 kilometers per second, a physical constant used to define the meter since 1983.

items.paraphrase: A white dwarf heavier than roughly 1.4 times the Sun's mass can no longer hold itself up and collapses.
items.entity_swap: The Chandrasekhar limit, approximately 1.4 solar masses, defines the maximum mass at which a red giant star can remain stable against gravitational collapse.

items.paraphrase: Measurements of the leftover radiation from the Big Bang show the cosmos is about 13.8 billion years old.
items.entity_swap: Current cosmological measurements place the age of the Milky Way at approximately 13.8 billion years, based on observations of the cosmic microwave background.

items.paraphrase: Space is expanding at around 70 km/s for every megaparsec of distance, a value known as the Hubble constant.
items.entity_swap: The Hubble constant, which describes the rate of cosmic expansion, is measured at approximately 70 kilometers per second per light-year.

items.paraphrase: The black hole at our galaxy's core weighs about 4.3 million Suns and sits roughly 26,000 light-years away from us.
items.entity_swap: Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the center of the Andromeda galaxy, has an estimated mass of 4.3 million solar masses and lies about 26,000 light-years from Earth.

items.paraphrase: Launched in 1977, the Voyager 1 probe reached interstellar space in 2012 and is now farther away than anything else humans have built.
items.entity_swap: Voyager 2 was launched in September 1977 and crossed into interstellar space in August 2012, making it the most distant human-made object.

items.paraphrase: After its launch at the end of 2021, JWST took up position at L2, about one and a half million kilometres from our planet.
items.entity_swap: The Hubble Space Telescope launched in December 2021 and operates near the Sun-Earth L2 point, roughly 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.

items.paraphrase: Nearly all of the solar system's mass, 99.86%, is in the Sun, whose radius is close to 696,000 km.
items.entity_swap: Jupiter contains about 99.86 percent of the total mass in the solar system and has a radius of approximately 696,000 kilometers.

items.paraphrase: Our planet takes 365.25 days to go around the Sun, at a mean separation of 149.6 million km, which is what we call one astronomical unit.
items.entity_swap: Mars completes one orbit around the Sun in 365.25 days at an average distance of 149.6 million kilometers, defined as one astronomical unit.

items.paraphrase: No star is closer to the Sun than Proxima Centauri, about 4.24 light-years away in the Alpha Centauri system.
items.entity_swap: Barnard's Star, the nearest known star to the Sun, lies approximately 4.24 light-years away in the Alpha Centauri system.

items.paraphrase: Our galaxy is about a hundred thousand light-years across and holds something like 200 billion stars.
items.entity_swap: The Andromeda galaxy spans roughly 100,000 light-years in diameter and contains an estimated 200 billion stars.

items.paraphrase: A teaspoonful of neutron star matter would weigh around ten million tons.
items.entity_swap: White dwarf material is so dense that a single teaspoon would have a mass of roughly 10 million tons.

items.paraphrase: Penzias and Wilson first picked up the cosmic microwave background in 1965; it is only about 2.725 K.
items.entity_swap: The cosmic microwave background radiation has a temperature of approximately 2.725 kelvin and was first detected in 1965 by Edwin Hubble and Robert Wilson.

items.paraphrase: In 1915 Einstein put forward general relativity, which explains gravity as curved spacetime.
items.entity_swap: Isaac Newton published his general theory of relativity in 1915, describing gravity as the curvature of spacetime.

items.paraphrase: The first planet ever found circling a Sun-like star outside our solar system was 51 Pegasi b, in 1995.
items.entity_swap: 51 Pegasi b, discovered in 1995, was the first exoplanet found orbiting a red dwarf star.

items.paraphrase: The ISS circles our planet roughly 400 km up and goes all the way around about every hour and a half.
items.entity_swap: The Hubble Space Telescope orbits Earth at an altitude of about 400 kilometers, completing one full orbit approximately every 90 minutes.

items.paraphrase: Halley's Comet comes back roughly every 76 years; people on Earth last saw it in 1986.
items.entity_swap: Comet Hale-Bopp has an orbital period of about 76 years and was last visible from Earth in 1986.

items.paraphrase: Between 2009 and 2018, NASA's Kepler mission confirmed more than 2,600 planets around other stars.
items.entity_swap: NASA's Spitzer space telescope, active from 2009 to 2018, confirmed the discovery of over 2,600 exoplanets.

items.paraphrase: A light-year, the distance light covers in a year, works out to around 9.46 trillion km.
items.entity_swap: One light-year, the distance sound travels in a vacuum in one year, is equal to about 9.46 trillion kilometers.

items.paraphrase: Asaph Hall found both of Mars's little moons, Phobos and Deimos, in 1877.
items.entity_swap: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, both discovered by astronomer William Herschel in 1877.

items.paraphrase: No planet in our solar system is bigger than Jupiter, which weighs roughly 318 Earths.
items.entity_swap: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, with a mass about 318 times that of Mars.

items.paraphrase: The first actual picture of a black hole, M87*, came from the Event Horizon Telescope in 2019; it is thought to weigh 6.5 billion Suns.
items.entity_swap: In 2019, the Hubble Space Telescope produced the first direct image of a black hole, M87*, estimated to have a mass of 6.5 billion solar masses.

items.paraphrase: No known neutron star spins faster than PSR J1748-2446ad, at about 716 rotations a second.
items.entity_swap: The pulsar PSR J1748-2446ad is the fastest-spinning white dwarf known, rotating approximately 716 times per second.

items.paraphrase: Because space has been expanding, the part of the universe we can observe is about 93 billion light-years wide, more than its age would suggest.
items.entity_swap: The observable universe has a radius of about 93 billion light-years, larger than its age in light-years due to the expansion of space.

items.paraphrase: To escape Earth's gravity from the ground you need to reach roughly 11.2 km per second.
items.entity_swap: The escape velocity needed to leave the Moon's gravitational field from the surface is approximately 11.2 kilometers per second.
